mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals tightening monetary policy that raises discount rates and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is rising, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.0% and remains above this level for two consecutive months, it triggers a restrictive monetary policy that depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The signal triggers (FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for 2 months) but 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening policy amid a strong labor market, which suppresses corporate earnings growth and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening policy with strong labor market
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE falling) occurs but 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle defined by rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and declining industrial production (INDPRO), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced economic growth and profit visibility.
failure_condition: The regime condition (FEDFUNDS rising and INDPRO falling) is met but 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC for the regime condition falls below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS is rising, or Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1250 thousand units for two consecutive months, it signals weakening residential demand that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The signal triggers (HOUST < 1250 for 2 months) but 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate profit growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO is rising, or Rank IC over the last 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion defined by high consumer credit (RSAFS > 500,000 million dollars) and strong GDP (GDPC1 > 17,000 billion dollars), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to overvaluation and policy tightening concerns.
failure_condition: The regime condition (RSAFS > 500000 and GDPC1 > 17000) is met but 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC for the regime condition falls below 0.02.
